Recommendations for Video Improvement

LATE VISUAL

"process follows simple" (segment 2): visual appears 9.3s after narration. Show the slide BEFORE or during the explanation, not after.

VOCABULARY MISMATCH

21 keywords use different terminology than what appears on screen. Consider adding the spoken terms to slide text, or using consistent vocabulary.

PACING

31% of matched visuals were on screen 10+ seconds before narration. Consider restructuring slides to appear closer to when the narrator discusses them.

Methodology

What Temporal Contiguity (TC) Measures

TC measures whether visual content is displayed simultaneously with the corresponding narration. Based on Mayer & Moreno's Temporal Contiguity Principle: "Students learn better when corresponding words and pictures are presented simultaneously rather than successively."

What TC Does NOT Measure

  • Visual quality or clarity of slides
  • Pedagogical effectiveness of the content itself
  • Whether abstract narration SHOULD have visual support
  • Student learning outcomes (TC is a design principle, not a learning measure)

Why Coverage Rate != TC Score

The TC Score (e.g., 92.35) measures temporal alignment quality among concepts that DO have visual correlates. The Coverage Rate (e.g., 32.6%) measures what fraction of narrated concepts have any visual support at all. These are different metrics:

  • A video where the narrator says "imagine a foggy landscape" has no visual that SHOULD exist for this metaphor. Excluding it from TC is correct.
  • A video where the narrator says "this algorithm" while a diagram is on screen IS a TC measurement.
  • The Coverage-Adjusted score (TC x Coverage) is a composite metric, not a standard TC metric.

Alignment Cases Explained

A Visual on screen: The keyword text is found in the current scene's OCR. The visual was already present when the narrator spoke. Score = 100 (no penalty).
D Progressive reveal: The keyword appears mid-scene (not from the start). Common for animated slides. Still present at narration time. Score = 100.
B Visual appears late: The keyword is not on screen at narration time but appears within +10 seconds. Score penalized by Gaussian/piecewise formula.
C Visual expired: The keyword was shown earlier but has disappeared. Maximum penalty (delta_t capped at 10s).
G SigLIP match: No text match, but visual similarity detected (animations, diagrams without labels). Reduced confidence (alpha < 0.5).
F No visual correlate: No matching visual found. Excluded from TC scoring. Sub-reasons: no_ocr_nearby (talking head), ocr_vocabulary_mismatch (different terms), low_groundability (abstract concept).

Asymmetric Scoring

delta_t = t_vis - t_narr. Only positive delta_t is penalized (visual appears AFTER narration). Negative delta_t means the visual was already showing = no penalty. This is correct per TC theory: having the visual prepared ahead of narration is good instructional design.

Confidence Tiers

  • HIGH (alpha = 1.0): Full OCR phrase match in the scene
  • MEDIUM (alpha = 0.8): Partial word-level OCR match (at least one content word found)
  • LOW (alpha < 0.5): SigLIP visual similarity match (no text evidence)
